'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Pokrovsk offensive]]
***Hundreds of [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian troops]] enter the city of [[Pokrovsk]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]] with heavy [[urban warfare|street-to-street]] fighting underway. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/moscows-forces-push-south-ukrainian-city-kupiansk-russian-commander-says-2025-11-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Islamabad suicide bombing]]
**Twelve people are killed and 27 injured in a [[Suicide attack|suicide bombing]] outside a [[Judiciary of Pakistan|court]] in [[Islamabad]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/11/blast-outside-islamabad-court-in-pakistan-injures-at-least-eight (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israeli settler violence]]
**[[Israeli settlers]] [[arson|set fire]] to dozens of vehicles and other property in [[Beit Lid]] and [[Deir Sharaf]] in the [[West Bank]] and attack [[Israeli soldiers]] who were dispatched to the area, injuring four [[Palestinians]], while four [[Israelis]] are arrested. [https://www.dw.com/en/israeli-settlers-set-fire-to-west-bank-mosque/a-74736695 (DW)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Turkish Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash]]
**Twenty people are killed when a [[Turkish Air Force]] [[Lockheed C-130 Hercules|C-130 Hercules]] [[cargo aircraft|cargo plane]] crashes near the [[Azerbaijan–Georgia border]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2025/11/11/turkish-military-c-130-cargo-plane-crashes-in-georgia-after-taking-off-from-azerbaijan (Euronews)] [https://apnews.com/article/turkey-plane-azerbaijan-georgia-crash-military-cargo-bcc35b26c66287f55b73cc11139dd3b4 (AP)]
*[[Electricity sector in the Dominican Republic]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]] experiences a rare countrywide [[power outage|blackout]], which officials blame on a failure in the [[electric power transmission|power transmission]] [[electrical grid|grid]]. [https://apnews.com/article/dominican-republic-blackout-power-outage-e0ea4742ae57fe4b13896a3c82284b41 (AP)]
*Twenty people are injured when three [[Domingo Faustino Sarmiento Railway|Sarmiento trains]] derail in [[Liniers]], [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]]. [https://tn.com.ar/sociedad/2025/11/11/descarrilo-una-formacion-del-tren-sarmiento-en-la-estacion-liniers/ (Todos Noticias <small>in Spanish</small>)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Colombia–United States relations]], [[2025 United States military strikes on alleged drug traffickers]]
**[[Colombia]]n [[President of Colombia|president]] [[Gustavo Petro]] orders [[Public Forces (Colombia)|public forces]] to halt [[intelligence sharing]] with the [[United States Intelligence Community]] until the [[U.S.]] ceases its [[military strike]]s on vessels in the [[Caribbean Sea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/colombia-president-orders-suspension-intelligence-sharing-with-us-2025-11-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Japan–Russia relations]], [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russia]] indefinitely bans 30 [[Japanese nationality law|Japanese nationals]], including a [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|foreign ministry]] official, from entering the country in response to Japan's sanctions on Russian entities over [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|the war]] in [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/russia-bars-30-japanese-individuals-response-ukraine-sanctions-2025-11-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2006 Noida serial murders]]
**The [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] of [[India]] acquits Surendra Koli of all remaining charges in the [[Serial killer|series of child murders]] and [[Rape|rapes]] which occurred between 2005 and 2006 in [[Noida]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], and ordering his immediate release. Koli was originally [[Capital punishment in India|sentenced to death]] and was serving a [[life sentence]] for the remaining cases. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/nithari-killings-supreme-court-acquits-prime-accused-surendra-koli-in-last-pending-case/article70265652.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*[[2024 South Korean martial law crisis]]
**A [[High courts of South Korea|high court]] in [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], issues an [[arrest warrant]] for former [[National Intelligence Service (South Korea)|National Intelligence Service]] director [[Cho Tae-yong]] for allegedly [[tampering with evidence]] regarding former [[President of South Korea|president]] [[Yoon Suk Yeol]]'s declaration of [[martial law]], among other charges. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-court-issued-arrest-warrant-former-spy-agency-chief-under-probe-2025-11-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Turkish football betting scandal]]
**A [[Judicial system of Turkey|court]] in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]], issues arrest warrants for eight suspects involved in an investigation into alleged illegal [[sports betting]] by [[Turkish Football Federation]] [[referee]]s, [[List of football clubs in Turkey|club]] presidents, and [[footballer|player]]s. [https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-football-betting-scandal-arrest-warrants-issued/a-74698309 (DW)]
*[[Anti-war protests in Russia (2022–present)|Anti-war protests in Russia]]
**A [[Judiciary of Russia|court]] in [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Russia]], extends [[street musician]] [[Diana Loginova]]'s [[Prisons in Russia|detention]] for 13 days for allegedly [[Public-order crime|violating public order]] during an October performance that included [[Anti-war movement|anti-war]] [[List of anti-war songs|songs]], marking her third consecutive sentence since mid-October. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-street-singer-arrest-44d922d3477b0bba75abef3371627c0a (AP)]
*[[Corruption in Ukraine]]
**The [[National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine]] starts investigating a large-scale [[corruption]] scheme in the country’s [[Electricity in Ukraine|energy sector]], involving the state nuclear power operator [[Energoatom]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2025/11/11/ukraines-anti-corruption-watchdog-probes-alleged-energy-sector-scheme (EuroNews)]
*A [[Gabon]]ese [[Politics of Gabon#Judicial branch|court]] sentences former [[First ladies and gentlemen of Gabon|first lady]] [[Sylvia Bongo Ondimba]] and her son, [[Noureddin Bongo Valentin]], to 20 years in prison each for receiving and [[Embezzlement|embezzling]] public funds, among other charges. Both were [[Trial in absentia|tried in absentia]] as they live in exile. [https://www.barrons.com/news/gabon-court-sentences-ex-leader-s-wife-and-son-to-20-years-in-jail-for-graft-f5e39f21 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*The [[Southwark Crown Court]] in [[London]], [[United Kingdom]], sentences [[Chinese people|Chinese]] [[fraud]]ster [[Qian Zhimin (criminal)|Qian Zhimin]] to 11 years and eight months in [[Prisons in the United Kingdom|prison]] for running a [[Ponzi scheme]] that [[Cryptocurrency and crime|defrauded]] over 128,000 investors and [[Money laundering|laundered]] the proceeds into [[Bitcoin]], resulting in the recovery of about ₿61,000 in the country's largest [[cryptocurrency]] seizure. [https://apnews.com/article/uk-china-cryptoqueen-bitcoin-fraud-b115ccc6e98f015dad01fa75d6ce0cf7 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Iraqi parliamentary election]]
**[[Iraqis]] vote to elect the 329 members of the [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Council of Representatives]], who will elect [[Iraq|the country]]'s [[President of Iraq|president]] and approve the president's appointment of a [[Prime Minister of Iraq|prime minister]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/iraq-vote-turnout-more-than-55-sharply-up-on-2021-fe90fb49 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[2025 Irish presidential election]]
**[[Catherine Connolly]] is sworn in as the 10th [[president of Ireland]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cnveplv3lzmo (BBC News)]
*[[Gun law in New Zealand]]
**[[New Zealand]] announces the transfer of [[Firearms license|gun licensing]] responsibilities from [[New Zealand Police|the police]] to an independent Firearms Safety Authority reporting directly to [[New Zealand Government|the government]]. [https://apnews.com/article/christchurch-shooting-guns-new-zealand-semiautomatic-ban-f370885a43616f652410fe6d94768ef2 (AP)]
*Thousands of people protest in [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]], against the proposed re-development of the former [[Yugoslav People's Army]] [[General Staff Building, Belgrade|General Staff Building]], which was delisted as a [[heritage asset|cultural asset]] last year. [https://www.dw.com/en/serbs-protest-kushner-backed-belgrade-project-at-army-site/a-74702710 (DW)]

'''Science and technology'''
